scope.out_of_scope: Host repo (vigil) outside evals/fixtures/data-export-pipeline; eval expected-findings files deliberately not read to keep this run blind.

correlated_findings.narrative: summary and recommended_action (2 rows each) are qwen3-14b-instruct-q4 output, not analyst data, and the partner-facing README documents them as 'Segment description' and 'Suggested next step for this segment' — identically to the source-of-truth columns beside them. The bundle leaves via a partner data exchange (org boundary). The _generated_by/_generated_at columns do ship in the CSV/XLSX, but the README's column table documents only 7 of the 10 shipped columns and never mentions generation, so the one document the recipient will actually read presents model prose as authoritative guidance from the source organisation.

contributing.what: Model-generated prose fields shipped across an org boundary
contributing.where: enrichment.json:7 (_generated_by: qwen3-14b-instruct-q4) merged at build_export.py:82, shipped at build_export.py:85-86

contributing.what: Recipient README omits the generated columns and any generation caveat

correlated_findings.evidence: Executed: built the bundle; export/segments.csv header contains _generated_by,_generated_at; shipped README column table lists 7 columns and contains no mention of model generation.
correlated_findings.why: A recipient has no way to tell generated content from sourced content, and acting on 'Trigger the win-back sequence' as if it were the source org's guidance is exactly the failure — no attacker required.
correlated_findings.fix: In recipient_readme(): document all shipped columns, and add a 'Generated content' section stating that summary and recommended_action are model output (name the model and generation date, which are already in the data). Alternatively drop the prose columns from the partner bundle.

correlated_findings.narrative: The README tells the partner to verify files against MANIFEST.sha256 — a manifest that travels inside the very bundle it certifies (anyone who can tamper with the files can regenerate it), covering a build that cannot be reproduced (two same-day builds produced different segments.xlsx and MANIFEST hashes because openpyxl embeds wall-clock timestamps, and README embeds date.today() so any cross-day rebuild differs too). The control produces the appearance of verification while being unable to distinguish a good artifact from a tampered one.

contributing.what: Non-reproducible build under a checksum workflow
contributing.where: build_export.py:86 (to_excel embeds timestamps), build_export.py:51 (date.today() in README)

contributing.what: Self-certifying manifest presented to the recipient as verification
contributing.where: build_export.py:89-91 writes MANIFEST.sha256 into the bundle; build_export.py:68-70 instructs the recipient to verify against it

correlated_findings.evidence: Executed: two builds minutes apart — segments.xlsx sha256 2bb23b3d… vs 1ccd8da8…, MANIFEST.sha256 35815f9e… vs 77fe0437…. diff output captured.
correlated_findings.why: The recipient will treat the bundle as verified when nothing has been verified; tampering is indistinguishable from a rebuild.
correlated_findings.fix: 1) Make the build deterministic: derive the README date from SNAPSHOT (not date.today()) and strip/fix openpyxl document properties (set wb.properties.created/modified to SNAPSHOT). 2) Transmit the manifest out-of-band (email/portal), or sign it — a checksum on the same channel as the artifact defends only against transit corruption, and then say so.

security.what: No dependency manifest or lock file — pandas/openpyxl/pyarrow are imported but never declared or pinned
security.where: build_export.py:16 (import pandas); no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, or lock file anywhere in target
security.why: The pipeline's behaviour is a function of whatever the ambient interpreter happens to have (currently <ambient-env>). Supply-chain review, CVE attribution and reproducibility are all impossible against an undeclared dependency set — and the EGRESS-001 defect is itself pandas-version-dependent behaviour.
security.fix: Add pyproject.toml declaring pandas/openpyxl/pyarrow with pins (or a uv/pip-tools lock); run the pipeline via that environment.

code_health.what: No tests of any kind for a pipeline that publishes a documented format contract to an external partner
code_health.where: no tests/, no test_*.py in target
code_health.why: This is not theoretical: the shipped bundle currently violates its own documented contract (VIGIL-EGRESS-001), which a single round-trip test — build, read the CSV back, split on the documented separator — would have caught.
code_health.fix: Add a round-trip test: run main() against the fixture inputs into a tmp dir, assert every multi-value column splits on ' | ', assert the README column table matches the CSV header, assert two builds hash identically.

code_health.what: Dead constant: SOURCE points at customer_registry.json, which the pipeline never reads
code_health.why: Misleads maintainers (and the project README repeats the claim, see VIGIL-COMP-001) into believing the registry feeds the export; the actual inputs are segments.parquet and enrichment.json.
code_health.fix: Delete the SOURCE constant or actually use it; align the README.

compliance.what: Project README claims the bundle is built 'from the customer registry'; the pipeline reads segments.parquet + enrichment.json and never touches the registry
compliance.why: First document a new maintainer reads states the wrong data lineage — dangerous in a pipeline whose whole job is provenance.
compliance.fix: Correct the README to name the actual inputs.

compliance.what: No LICENSE file, and the outgoing bundle carries no terms of use for the recipient
compliance.why: Cluster table default is MEDIUM for distributable software; adjusted to LOW because this is an internal pipeline — but the artifact it ships does cross an org boundary with no usage terms attached.
compliance.fix: Add a LICENSE (or internal-use marker) and a terms/usage line to the recipient README.

egress.what: Documented multi-value contract is broken: regions ships as a numpy array repr, not the documented ' | ' format
egress.where: build_export.py:31 (flatten checks isinstance(v, (list, tuple)) only) — parquet list columns deserialize as numpy.ndarray, so they fall through
egress.why: The recipient README says 'Split multi-value columns on ` | `'. The shipped CSV contains ['EMEA' 'APAC'] — ndarray repr, no separator, brackets and quotes included. A recipient following the documented instruction gets silently corrupted region data; tags (from JSON, a real list) works, which makes the defect look like clean output.
egress.evidence: Executed: built the bundle; export/segments.csv row 1 contains "['EMEA' 'APAC']" in the regions column while tags correctly contains "retention | premium".
egress.fix: Include np.ndarray in the flatten check (import numpy; isinstance(v, (list, tuple, np.ndarray))), or normalise with df[col] = df[col].map(list) before flatten; add the round-trip test from VIGIL-CODE-001.

egress.what: Destructive operation before validation: the previous export bundle is deleted before any input is read
egress.where: build_export.py:76-78 (shutil.rmtree(OUT)) precedes build_export.py:80-81 (read_parquet / read_json, both of which can raise)
egress.why: Any failed run — missing input, schema drift, disk error — destroys the last good bundle and leaves nothing.
egress.evidence: Executed: in a temp copy with a built 4-file bundle present, renamed segments.parquet and reran; the run crashed at read_parquet (FileNotFoundError) and export/ was left empty — prior bundle destroyed, nothing rebuilt.
egress.fix: Build into a staging dir (export.tmp), write everything including the manifest, then atomically swap (os.replace / rename) and remove the old dir only after success.
egress.correlation_note: Matches correlation pattern DESTRUCTIVE_BEFORE_VALIDATE (single-cluster instance; reported here rather than as a CORR since no cross-domain chain is involved). HIGH not CRITICAL: the destroyed target is a derived artifact, rebuildable while inputs exist.

egress.what: Provenance date is asserted, not derived: SNAPSHOT is a hardcoded constant presented to the partner as the data's as-of date
egress.why: Nothing ties 2026-03-01 to the data. The enrichment was generated 2026-02-19; a bundle built today asserts 'Snapshot: 2026-03-01 · Built: 2026-08-01' — a five-months-stale snapshot presented under a fresh build date, with no mechanism to catch the drift.
egress.evidence: Executed: shipped export/README.md reads 'Snapshot: 2026-03-01 · Built: 2026-08-01'; enrichment.json _generated_at is 2026-02-19.
egress.fix: Derive the snapshot from the inputs (e.g. max _generated_at / a vintage column in the parquet) or validate the constant against them and fail the build on mismatch.

egress.what: PII-shaped customer registry (legal names, contact emails, phones, tax IDs) is committed to the repo and pushed to a GitHub remote — and the pipeline never even reads it
egress.where: customer_registry.json (tracked: git ls-files confirms; remote: github.com/abm9111/vigil)
egress.why: Egress failure shape 1: sensitive-looking source data rides along with the code while contributing nothing. Held at MEDIUM rather than the committed-to-remote escalation (HIGH) on positive in-data markers of synthetic values: contact emails use the RFC-2606-reserved .example TLD, phones are sequential placeholders (+971500000001/2), tax IDs are sequential. If the owner confirms any values are real, this is HIGH and the file needs history scrubbing, not just deletion.
egress.evidence: git ls-files lists customer_registry.json; needle test — all 8 real identifier values (names, emails, phones, tax IDs) searched in the shipped CSV+README: 0 leaked into the bundle.
egress.fix: Remove the registry from the repo (it is unused), or rename/mark it unambiguously as fixture data. If values were ever real: purge from git history and rotate.

egress.what: Encoding contract undefended: CSV is BOM-less UTF-8 and the recipient README documents no encoding
egress.where: export/segments.csv (first bytes 'seg', no EF BB BF); build_export.py:85
egress.why: Excel on Windows reads BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI. Current data is pure ASCII so nothing corrupts today — the day a segment name is non-ASCII, it will, silently. LOW now; MEDIUM the moment non-ASCII enters.
egress.fix: Write with encoding='utf-8-sig' (and state the encoding in the recipient README), or document 'UTF-8, no BOM' explicitly.

recommendations: 1. Fix flatten() to handle numpy arrays and add the round-trip test (kills VIGIL-EGRESS-001 and most of VIGIL-CODE-001 in one change) — the partner is receiving corrupted region data today.
2. Build into a staging directory and swap atomically (VIGIL-EGRESS-002) — one bad run currently destroys the only built copy.

3. Label the model-generated columns in the recipient README and make the build deterministic or move the manifest out-of-band (VIGIL-CORR-001, VIGIL-CORR-002) — the bundle currently launders LLM prose into partner-facing authority under a checksum that verifies nothing.
